messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - GPU node flap detected in us-west-2 (n-gpu-77). Multiple inference containers terminated with CUDA illegal memory access. Pager: @amy_oncall. Details: https://redwood.incidents/1758001234

amy_oncall: Picking this up. Thanks for the alert. Any immediate customer-facing symptoms?

kai_sre: Seeing kubelet restarts on n-gpu-77. Node marked NotReady repeatedly. Logs show OOM followed by driver errors complaining about illegal memory access.

jordy_runtime: Runtime logs (snippet) show repeated kernel/device faults: 
```
E Cuda: illegal memory access at address 0x7f8a12bff000
#0  runtime::gpu::launch_kernel+0x2a
#1  runtime::kv_cache::apply+0x1f
#2  runtime::serve::request_loop+0x4b
```

amy_oncall: How many requests failing? Any specific models or tenants?

jordy_runtime: Error rate spiked to ~7% from 0.1% over ~6m for service rtr:inference-prod. Tenants on that node: tenant-17, tenant-23, tenant-88, tenant-118, tenant-alloc-a. Two mid-tier customers saw retries and latency spikes.

nisha_customer-success: I'm standing by to notify customers. Do we need an immediate status page update?

leo_infra: Planning to cordon + drain the node:
```
kubectl cordon n-gpu-77
kubectl drain n-gpu-77 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

kai_sre: Hold on. Don't drain yet — we need to capture kernel dmesg and /var/log/nvidia before we evict pods or logs rotate. If we lose dmesg we lose forensic evidence.

amy_oncall: Leo, run a quick snapshot (dmesg, nv-smi logs) and upload artifacts, then cordon. Also set PD ticket if not already.

leo_infra: Snapshot taken and uploaded: s3://incidents/1758001234/artifacts/dmesg.txt. I'll cordon in 45s.

ops-bot: PD incident created PD-INC-7891 severity=sev2 assignee=@amy_oncall

amy_oncall: Starting controlled migration: migrate low-priority pods first, keep critical services pinned to alternate nodes where possible. Also switching fallback model variants for critical tenants to small-quantized to reduce memory pressure.

jordy_runtime: Observed pattern: container OOM -> GPU driver illegal access shortly after. Hypothesis: eviction/paging race where GPU driver attempts to access pages being reclaimed, leading to misaligned device addresses. Memory limiting prevents OOM but not the underlying kernel/device coordination issue.

kai_sre: Escalating to NVIDIA with traces. Attached full trace bundle to PD and S3.

nisha_customer-success: Posting interim status update to status.redwood.ai: affected customers being notified; ETA to stabilize ~20-30m assuming drain/migration works. Will escalate to account teams for worried customers.

amy_oncall: If migration doesn't reduce errors, fallback plan: rollout runtime patch 1.3.5-hotpatch that preflushes KV caches before eviction. Canary to 10% traffic first. Jordy, can you push canary?

jordy_runtime: Pushing canary now:
```
kubectl set image deploy/runtime-canary runtime=registry.redwood/runtime:1.3.5-hotpatch
```
Monitoring logs for illegal mem access.

amy_oncall: Also increasing graceful eviction window to 45s to reduce race chance.

kai_sre: After cordon+snapshot we observed two other nodes with similar recent kernel versions and BIOS revisions. Suggest adding temporary nodeSelector to avoid hosts with BIOS < 1.2.7 while we investigate.

leo_infra: Cordon+drain executed. Eviction completed. Pods rescheduled onto healthy nodes. Observability: error rate down to ~0.6%, latency returning to baseline for most endpoints.

nisha_customer-success: Customer updates sent. No reports of data loss — symptoms were retries and delayed responses; we flagged logs for any corrupted output but nothing found so far.

amy_oncall: Leaving PD open for 1h of post-mitigation monitoring. Filed long-term tasks: vendor escalation, kernel regression test, and improved pre-eviction flush.

jordy_runtime: Filed bug RU-1423 to track hotpatch, kernel workaround, and memstress + GPU regression tests. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.local/browse/RU-1423

amy_oncall: TL;DR: probable kernel/page-eviction race causing misaligned device address/cuda illegal memory access after OOMs. Mitigations: snapshot + cordon, drain + migrate, hotpatch canary, increase eviction grace, notify customers. Next steps: postmortem + upstream vendor engagement.

nisha_customer-success: I'll follow up with PS teams and post incident summary on the status page after the watch window.

incidents-bot: Incident update posted: https://redwood.incidents/1758001234/update-1
